body:
### Summary I'm trying to have uv stop using `%APPDATA%\uv` altogether, and for some reason, this seems to be the only hardcoded path left that I know about. While I am aware that the `UV_PYTHON` variable that can fulfill the same functionality, it's problematic when trying to upgrade tools. It will try to migrate the tool to that version when upgrading because it's the same as using the parameter. However, when using a global pin, it will not try to use that version when upgrading, it will only do that when installing a new tool (unless you override it with `UV_PYTHON` or `-p`). Found this out the hard way when running `uv tool upgrade --all`, ended up having to reinstall quite a bit of my tools because it tried to migrate them to freethreaded and failed.
My original reasoning (not as pressing) Months from now, I could forget that the global pin is hard-coded and try to use the command again. I'm sure there are probably edge-cases with precedence to consider as well. It's also more convenient in comparison to be able to just use `uv python pin --global`
### Example `$env:UV_PYTHON_GLOBAL_PIN_FILE = "C:\example\path\.python-version"`
title: Global python pin file environment variable
